entries.title: I Samuel 12:2
segments: Those who serve God from their childhood are often made distinguished benefactors to mankind.

entries.title: I Samuel 12:4
segments:
Taken aught; any thing wrongfully. 
 
Men who have long been in public life, and have been governed by the fear and love of God, may expect when they retire to leave a conviction of their fidelity in the hearts of others, which shall tend greatly to promote his glory and the good of their fellow men.

entries.title: I Samuel 12:6
segments: Aged men, after retiring from more laborious and active duties, may still be useful by communicating to the young a knowledge of facts in the history of their fathers, and of the instructions which those facts afford.

entries.title: I Samuel 12:10
segments: A just review of the past will impress the conviction that sin leads to misery, and that there is no escaping it, except in repentance and hearty devotion to the service of God.

entries.title: I Samuel 12:11
segments: Bedan; perhaps either Barak or Abdon.

entries.title: I Samuel 12:12
segments: That Nahash--came; the attack of Nahash upon Jabesh-Gilead took place after Saul had been anointed king; but he had previously threatened the Israelites, and the fear of him was with them a chief motive for asking of Samuel a king to go before them and fight their battles.

entries.title: I Samuel 12:15
segments: However great the blessings which God bestows upon a people, they cannot long preserve them unless they hearken to his voice and walk in his ways.

entries.title: I Samuel 12:18
segments: The Lord sent thunder and rain; an uncommon thing, as it ordinarily never rained in Palestine during the season of wheat-harvest.

entries.title: I Samuel 12:19
segments: The true friends of God can greatly benefit their fellow men; and often the wicked in their distress feel this, and apply to them for help.

entries.title: I Samuel 12:23
segments: However ungratefully pious men may have been treated, they will labor to do good even to those who have done them evil; while they maintain that there can be no real blessedness but in hearty obedience to the commands of God.
